description: Version 2: original v1 preserved. Four development regressions, three previously evaluated untouched cases, and three fresh authored holdouts. Gold fixed before second live evaluation; all groups must be reported separately.

items.title: Security advisory: Critical remote code execution vulnerabilities, update now
items.summary: PHP 8.5.12、8.4.27、8.3.36 和 8.2.35 修复了两个可导致未认证远程代码执行的漏洞：一个涉及内存耗尽时请求数据未完全初始化，另一个涉及工作进程后续请求使用已释放内存中的陈旧状态。所有处理网页请求的 PHP 安装都可能受影响；公告称 mod_php 风险最高，并展示了可在应用代码运行前触发的攻击。无法立即更新时，配置调整只能降低特定攻击路径的风险，不能替代升级。

items.title: PHP 8.2.35
items.summary: PHP 8.2.35 是 PHP 开发团队发布的安全更新，修复了两个可能导致未认证远程代码执行的严重漏洞（CVE-2026-109618、CVE-2026-109619）。公告称没有完整的缓解措施，并强烈建议 PHP 8.2 用户立即更新；PHP 8.2 将于 2026 年 12 月 31 日终止支持，之后不再获得安全修复。

items.title: Today's PHP security release, and how we're strengthening security
items.summary: PHP 项目已发布 PHP 8.5.12、8.4.27、8.3.36 和 8.2.35，修复两项严重漏洞；在特定条件下，这些漏洞可让未认证攻击者在运行 PHP 的服务器上执行代码。文章称，其中一个内存管理问题早在 2024 年审计期间就露出迹象，但修复因兼容性、性能和扩展生态的取舍，以及安全团队决策和资源不足而多次停滞；2026 年 8 月研究人员报告了该问题的远程代码执行影响后，修复才成为首要任务。PHP 基金会称，已成立生态安全团队并开始调整决策流程，以便更快处理这类复杂漏洞。

cases.rationale: User-confirmed regression: security release duplicates advisory; foundation process investigation has independent value. Public generated summaries only; original bodies require an explicit local directory.

provenance.reason: Known development regression or adjudicated gold

items.title: Harbor bridge reopens Tuesday
items.summary: The harbor bridge reopens Tuesday after cable repairs.
items.evidence: The city confirms the harbor bridge reopens to all traffic Tuesday following repairs to damaged suspension cables.

items.title: Bridge reopening: repair findings and inspection rules
items.summary: The harbor bridge reopens Tuesday. Saltwater entered failed seals, corroding cable anchorages; crews replaced seals and added continuous moisture sensors. Monthly anchorage inspection replaces annual visual checks.
items.evidence: A city engineering report confirms Tuesday reopening. Laboratory examination found saltwater ingress through failed seals corroded anchorages. Crews replaced seals and installed moisture sensors with automatic alarms. Monthly inspections replace annual visual checks; emergency vehicle loading tests passed.

cases.rationale: The detailed report contains the brief announcement plus substantial mechanisms and new inspection policy. Keep richer coverage regardless of order.

items.title: Province reports drought crop losses
items.summary: Drought reduced this season's wheat harvest by 18%; the province opened emergency farm grants.
items.evidence: The provincial agriculture office reports an 18% wheat harvest reduction and emergency grants of up to 20,000 units per affected farm.

items.title: How wheat roots respond to drought
items.summary: A field study explains deeper root growth under water stress and shows that compaction limits access to retained subsoil moisture.
items.evidence: In the same drought-affected province, researchers excavated wheat roots from compacted and loosened plots. Water stress increased deep root growth in loose soils; compacted layers blocked the response. Loosening improved subsoil water uptake without increasing rainfall.

cases.rationale: Same drought context, independent economic impact and plant/soil mechanism.

items.title: Town water sample exceeds nitrate limit
items.summary: The town laboratory initially reported nitrate at 80 mg/L and issued a do-not-drink notice.
items.evidence: On Monday the municipal laboratory reported 80 mg/L nitrate in a water sample and issued an immediate do-not-drink notice pending confirmation.

items.title: Laboratory corrects nitrate result after unit error
items.summary: The laboratory corrected the concentration to 8 mg/L after a unit conversion error and rescinded the notice. Independent repeat samples confirmed the lower concentration.
items.evidence: On Tuesday the laboratory retracted Monday's 80 mg/L nitrate result. The instrument output had been multiplied by ten during unit conversion. The corrected value was 8 mg/L; independently collected repeat samples confirmed it. The town lifted its notice.

cases.rationale: Adjudicated after v1: correction article explicitly includes original 80 mg/L finding and notice, then explains unit conversion, corrected 8 mg/L, repeat samples and lifted notice. Original adds no independent fact. This does not mean corrections always replace earlier independent analysis.

provenance.reason: Known development regression or adjudicated gold
provenance.gold_change_from_v1: v1 wrongly required both articles; v2 keeps only complete correction. Original v1 data and scored results remain intact.

items.title: Rail reopening and track failure analysis
items.summary: The coastal line reopens Friday. A geotechnical report identifies drainage blockage and clay swelling as the cause of track displacement.
items.evidence: The railway confirms Friday reopening. Investigators traced track displacement to blocked drainage and swelling clay under the embankment. New drainage trenches and subgrade sensors address that failure mode.

items.title: Coastal rail line reopens Friday
items.summary: The railway says the coastal line will reopen Friday after repairs.
items.evidence: The coastal railway resumes regular passenger service Friday following repairs. No further engineering or operational details were supplied.

items.title: Reopening brings a different rail service plan
items.summary: The coastal line reopens Friday with timed bus connections, reserved bicycle spaces, and a six-week fare pilot.
items.evidence: For Friday's reopening the railway introduces guaranteed bus connections at two stations, reservable bicycle spaces, and a six-week off-peak fare pilot. These operational changes address commuter transfers and have no bearing on embankment repairs.

cases.rationale: Thin announcement overlaps either substantive article; failure analysis and operating plan provide separate value. Overlap must not transitively collapse all three.

items.title: Lagoon bloom shifts oxygen levels
items.summary: A bloom in Estuary Lagoon lowered dissolved oxygen to 2 mg/L at dawn. Researchers tracked the daily oxygen cycle and estimated that nutrient runoff sustained it.
items.evidence: Sampling during the Estuary Lagoon bloom found dawn dissolved oxygen of 2 mg/L and afternoon readings of 7 mg/L. Nutrient measurements and water-flow tracing linked the bloom to agricultural runoff. The team recommends intercepting runoff rather than relying on daytime oxygen readings.

items.title: Ferry operator changes lagoon routes during bloom
items.summary: The same Estuary Lagoon bloom clogged ferry cooling-water filters. The operator suspended two stops, added a replacement bus, and issued a new timetable.
items.evidence: The ferry operator says algae from the Estuary Lagoon bloom clogged raw-water engine filters. Two waterside stops are suspended until filters are replaced. Replacement buses run every twenty minutes and tickets remain valid. The notice contains no oxygen measurements or nutrient-source analysis.

cases.rationale: One environmental event, but ecological measurements/causes and passenger transport effects/actions have separate reading value.

items.title: Festival explains cancellation and refunds
items.summary: Friday evening's orchestra concert is canceled after inspectors found a fractured roof support. The hall is closed pending repairs; all tickets will be refunded automatically within ten days.
items.evidence: Festival organizers confirm the Friday evening orchestra concert is canceled and attendees should not travel to the venue. Inspectors found a fractured roof support at the hall, which will remain closed until structural repairs pass inspection. All ticket purchases will be refunded automatically to the original payment method within ten days. No replacement performance is planned.

cases.rationale: Followup explicitly includes every useful action/event fact from initial notice and adds safety cause, closure, and final refund procedure. Keep the complete notice regardless of input order.

items.title: Finches learn a color cue in laboratory task
items.summary: In a controlled trial, 40 finches learned a blue cue predicting food, averaging 82% correct choices after ten sessions. A reversal phase took three extra sessions and exposed side bias in eight birds.
items.evidence: Researchers trained forty finches with equal brightness blue and green cards. Blue predicted a food reward. Choices reached eighty-two percent correct after ten sessions. Reversing the rewarded color took three more sessions. Eight birds showed side bias; the authors report results both with and without those birds.

items.title: Outdoor finch trial finds no benefit from color cue
items.summary: A separate field trial found 51% correct choices when wild finches encountered color cues in daylight; changing illumination and unrestricted social feeding made the setup materially different from the laboratory task.
items.evidence: A field team tested untrained wild finches visiting outdoor feeders with blue and green signs. Of 210 observed feeder visits, 51 percent matched the nominal reward cue. Sun and shade changed sign brightness, and multiple birds could feed simultaneously. The authors say this is a separate ecological-validity test, not a retraction or repetition of the forty-bird training and reversal experiment.

cases.rationale: Shared animals, colors, and apparently conflicting success rates do not make separate experimental designs redundant. Each article supplies its own result and methods; neither contains the other experiment's independent details.
